evidence.claim: Oregon’s transportation department identifies this 66-mile scenic byway as a journey through five Western Oregon ecosystems, with access to rivers, reservoirs and trails.
evidence.quote: Along the way you'll pass through some of Oregon's oldest settlements, while experiencing the geographic diversity of five Western Oregon ecosystems.

evidence.claim: It gives a minimum driving time of two to three hours.

evidence.claim: Much of the drive parallels the Santiam Wagon Road, built to take settlers east to central Oregon pastures and gold mines in eastern Oregon and Idaho.
evidence.quote: Much of the Byway parallels the Santiam Wagon Road. Unlike most routes across the Cascades, this road was built to lead settlers away from the Willamette Valley to pasture lands in central Oregon, and to gold mines in eastern Oregon and Idaho.

evidence.claim: The toll road carried livestock and goods east and wool back to Willamette Valley mills.
evidence.quote: The Santiam Wagon Road was a vital means of supplying livestock and goods from western Oregon to central Oregon and transporting wool from east of the Cascades back to Willamette Valley woolen mills.

evidence.claim: Tolls ended in 1915, and the road passed to the state in 1925 for highway use.

flags: Current claim that the byway keeps to the wagon-road line was narrowed to parallels: ODOT uses that distinction, and the old freight route is not identical to the numbered highway or present byway.
ODOT gives no designation date or original byway campaign history. The documented wagon-road transition provides the road narrative. The 1905 race is supported but omitted for focus.

ODOT’s last-segment attraction order places Walton Ranch and Menagerie after the pass discussion; their geographic order is unclear in the prose. Omitted that sequence and used the supported river-to-pass-to-Hackleman progression.

Used Cascadia County Park because the park article documents the September 2022 ownership transfer. Older ODOT and town descriptions still say State Park. Cave ownership and access statements conflict internally; no cave access is promised.
Current Stand by Me Day wording omitted the 2020 interruption; corrected. Mineral-water benefits remain an attributed historical marketing claim. No other current claim was rejected as unsupported.

Crawfordsville Bridge is shorter because its cache gives a compact bridge history. No new coordinates or access promises added; current titles and coordinates retained. Current motifs fields were absent, so empty arrays supplied.
